page: Microsoft Azure F16as_v6 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Configured on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the server provides 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running a single thread per core on x86_64 architecture. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Architectural instruction support is extensive, featuring AVX-512 extensions (including VNNI and BF16) alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 64.0 GB RAM, delivering a resource ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Memory performance testing demonstrates robust throughput, scoring 2756.66 on PassMark memory benchmarks, with large-block memory read bandwidth achieving 75.97 GB/s and write bandwidth reaching 56.09 GB/s. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage and does not bundle dedicated GPUs, requiring network-attached block storage configurations for persistent operations and relying strictly on CPU resources for computation.

Benchmark evaluation shows exceptional single-threaded execution and data decompression capabilities. The instance achieved 2086.0 in single-core and 16516.0 in multi-core Geekbench tests, placing in the upper 25% of evaluated cloud servers. It also achieved top-tier throughput in small language model text generation (349.71 tokens/s for a 135M model) and strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 208.64 GB/s. Stress-ng multi-core and static web serving tests placed within the middle 50% percentile.

The 1:1 physical core-to-vCPU allocation ensures reliable processing capacity devoid of simultaneous multithreading contention. Due to its balanced memory footprint, strong single-core speed, and vector acceleration, the F16as_v6 is well suited for computational workflows, Clang software builds, lightweight CPU-based inference workloads, CI/CD pipelines, and application backends requiring stable processing cycles.
description: Microsoft Azure F16as_v6 is a compute-oriented virtual machine driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Providing 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture with one thread per core, it eliminates hyper-threading contention for consistent performance. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of memory (4.0 GB per core), 32 MB of L3 cache, and instruction support for AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16. The instance does not feature local storage or discrete GPUs, requiring external storage options for persistent data. In benchmark testing, the F16as_v6 demonstrates upper-quartile Geekbench scores (2086.0 single-core, 16516.0 multi-core) and superior performance in lightweight LLM inference and bzip3 decompression. This architecture is optimal for CPU-intensive compilation tasks, automated testing pipelines, lightweight AI inference, and backend application serving.
